To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the top of line condensation and corrosion is a complex phenomenon which is governed by the water condensation rate, temperature, iron carbonate precipitation rate, and the surface temperature.

(1) the TLC rate in stagnant gas conditions can be estimated by the new empirical model; (2) the TLC rate is influenced by the water condensation rate, the surface temperature and the presence of FeCO3 scale films on the steel surface; (3) the TLC rate can be predicted by the mechanistic model developed; (4) the TLC rate at stagnant gas velocity is influenced by the gas temperature, the gas flow velocity and the gas composition; (5) the mechanistic
TLC occurs when the temperature difference between the surface and bulk fluids is high enough to cause water to condense on the surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an understanding of TLC mechanisms, the development of a mechanistic model for TLC prediction and the evaluation of TLC control strategies.
the development of the experimental and theoretical models to predict the TLC in the CO2 environment.
the development of an understanding and predictive model of top of line corrosion and its mitigation by corrosion inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TLC is governed by the surface temperature and water condensation rate, whereas FeCO3 scale formation is influenced by the surface temperature, water condensation rate and the saturation of FeCO3.
the model was capable of predicting the top of the pipeline corrosion in the presence of FeCO3 scale.

the condensation of the water is the main factor that governs the corrosion at the upper surface of a pipeline, however, the precipitation of the FeCO3 and Fe3O4 films can significantly reduce the corrosion rate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TLC rate is governed by surface temperature and the WCR at temperatures below 32deg and 32degC above respectively.
the model can predict the corrosion rate and the thickness of corrosion product films at the top of line conditions.

the mechanistic model was able to reasonably predict the TLC rates at static conditions and it is a good starting point to further improve the mechanistic model for the prediction of TLC in the dynamic flow regime.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the condensation rate is the most influential parameter on TLC, followed by the surface temperature.
the TLC is governed by surface temperature, WCR and FeCO3 saturation.
the model is capable to predict the top of line conditions and the TLC rates at static conditions.
